shortDescription: Module to manage clusters in oVirt/RHV

options.name: auth
options.description: Dictionary with values needed to create HTTP/HTTPS connection to oVirt:

options.name: ballooning
options.description: If I(True) enable memory balloon optimization. Memory balloon is used to re-distribute / reclaim the host memory based on VM needs in a dynamic way.

options.name: comment
options.description: Comment of the cluster.

options.name: compatibility_version
options.description: The compatibility version of the cluster. All hosts in this cluster must support at least this compatibility version.

options.name: cpu_arch
options.description: CPU architecture of cluster.

options.name: cpu_type
options.description: CPU codename. For example I(Intel SandyBridge Family).

options.name: data_center
options.description: Datacenter name where cluster reside.

options.name: description
options.description: Description of the cluster.

options.name: external_network_providers
options.description: List of references to the external network providers available in the cluster. If the automatic deployment of the external network provider is supported, the networks of the referenced network provider are available on every host in the cluster. This is supported since oVirt version 4.2.

options.name: fence_connectivity_threshold
options.description: The threshold used by C(fence_skip_if_connectivity_broken).

options.name: fence_enabled
options.description: If I(True) enables fencing on the cluster. Fencing is enabled by default.

options.name: fence_skip_if_connectivity_broken
options.description: If I(True) fencing will be temporarily disabled if the percentage of hosts in the cluster that are experiencing connectivity issues is greater than or equal to the defined threshold. The threshold can be specified by C(fence_connectivity_threshold).

options.name: fence_skip_if_gluster_bricks_up
options.displayName: Fence Skip If Gluster Bricks Up
options.description: A flag indicating if fencing should be skipped if Gluster bricks are up and running in the host being fenced. This flag is optional, and the default value is `false`.

options.name: fence_skip_if_gluster_quorum_not_met
options.displayName: Fence Skip If Gluster Quorum Not Met
options.description: A flag indicating if fencing should be skipped if Gluster bricks are up and running and Gluster quorum will not be met without those bricks. This flag is optional, and the default value is `false`.

options.name: fence_skip_if_sd_active
options.description: If I(True) any hosts in the cluster that are Non Responsive and still connected to storage will not be fenced.

options.name: fetch_nested
options.description: If I(True) the module will fetch additional data from the API. It will fetch IDs of the VMs disks, snapshots, etc. User can configure to fetch other attributes of the nested entities by specifying C(nested_attributes).

options.name: firewall_type
options.description: The type of firewall to be used on hosts in this cluster. Up to version 4.1, it was always I(iptables). Since version 4.2, you can choose between I(iptables) and I(firewalld). For clusters with a compatibility version of 4.2 and higher, the default firewall type is I(firewalld).

options.name: gluster
options.description: If I(True), hosts in this cluster will be used as Gluster Storage server nodes, and not for running virtual machines. By default the cluster is created for virtual machine hosts.

options.name: gluster_tuned_profile
options.description: The name of the U(https://fedorahosted.org/tuned) to set on all the hosts in the cluster. This is not mandatory and relevant only for clusters with Gluster service. Could be for example I(virtual-host), I(rhgs-sequential-io), I(rhgs-random-io)

options.name: ha_reservation
options.description: If I(True) enables the oVirt/RHV to monitor cluster capacity for highly available virtual machines.

options.name: host_reason
options.description: If I(True) enables an optional reason field when a host is placed into maintenance mode from the Manager, allowing the administrator to provide an explanation for the maintenance.

options.name: id
options.description: ID of the cluster to manage.

options.name: ksm
options.description: I I(True) MoM enables to run Kernel Same-page Merging I(KSM) when necessary and when it can yield a memory saving benefit that outweighs its CPU cost.

options.name: ksm_numa
options.description: If I(True) enables KSM C(ksm) for best performance inside NUMA nodes.

options.name: mac_pool
options.description: MAC pool to be used by this cluster. C(Note:) This is supported since oVirt version 4.1.

options.name: memory_policy
options.description: I(disabled) - Disables memory page sharing. I(server) - Sets the memory page sharing threshold to 150% of the system memory on each host. I(desktop) - Sets the memory page sharing threshold to 200% of the system memory on each host.

options.name: migration_auto_converge
options.description: If I(True) auto-convergence is used during live migration of virtual machines. Used only when C(migration_policy) is set to I(legacy). Following options are supported: C(true) - Override the global setting to I(true). C(false) - Override the global setting to I(false). C(inherit) - Use value which is set globally.

options.name: migration_bandwidth
options.description: The bandwidth settings define the maximum bandwidth of both outgoing and incoming migrations per host. Following bandwidth options are supported: C(auto) - Bandwidth is copied from the I(rate limit) [Mbps] setting in the data center host network QoS. C(hypervisor_default) - Bandwidth is controlled by local VDSM setting on sending host. C(custom) - Defined by user (in Mbps).

options.name: migration_bandwidth_limit
options.description: Set the I(custom) migration bandwidth limit. This parameter is used only when C(migration_bandwidth) is I(custom).

options.name: migration_compressed
options.description: If I(True) compression is used during live migration of the virtual machine. Used only when C(migration_policy) is set to I(legacy). Following options are supported: C(true) - Override the global setting to I(true). C(false) - Override the global setting to I(false). C(inherit) - Use value which is set globally.

options.name: migration_encrypted
options.description: If I(True) encryption is used during live migration of the virtual machine. Following options are supported: C(true) - Override the global setting to I(true). C(false) - Override the global setting to I(false). C(inherit) - Use value which is set globally.

options.name: migration_policy
options.description: A migration policy defines the conditions for live migrating virtual machines in the event of host failure. Following policies are supported: C(legacy) - Legacy behavior of 3.6 version. C(minimal_downtime) - Virtual machines should not experience any significant downtime. C(suspend_workload) - Virtual machines may experience a more significant downtime. C(post_copy) - Virtual machines should not experience any significant downtime. options.name: name
options.description: Name of the cluster to manage.

options.name: nested_attributes
options.description: Specifies list of the attributes which should be fetched from the API. This parameter apply only when C(fetch_nested) is I(true).

options.name: network
options.description: Management network of cluster to access cluster hosts.

options.name: poll_interval
options.description: Number of the seconds the module waits until another poll request on entity status is sent.

options.name: resilience_policy
options.description: The resilience policy defines how the virtual machines are prioritized in the migration. Following values are supported: C(do_not_migrate) -  Prevents virtual machines from being migrated.  C(migrate) - Migrates all virtual machines in order of their defined priority. C(migrate_highly_available) - Migrates only highly available virtual machines to prevent overloading other hosts.

options.name: rng_sources
options.description: List that specify the random number generator devices that all hosts in the cluster will use. Supported generators are: I(hwrng) and I(random).

options.name: scheduling_policy
options.description: Name of the scheduling policy to be used for cluster.

options.name: scheduling_policy_properties
options.description: Custom scheduling policy properties of the cluster. These optional properties override the properties of the scheduling policy specified by the C(scheduling_policy) parameter.

options.name: serial_policy
options.description: Specify a serial number policy for the virtual machines in the cluster. Following options are supported: C(vm) - Sets the virtual machine's UUID as its serial number. C(host) - Sets the host's UUID as the virtual machine's serial number. C(custom) - Allows you to specify a custom serial number in C(serial_policy_value).

options.name: serial_policy_value
options.description: Allows you to specify a custom serial number. This parameter is used only when C(serial_policy) is I(custom).

options.name: spice_proxy
options.description: The proxy by which the SPICE client will connect to virtual machines. The address must be in the following format: I(protocol://[host]:[port])

options.name: state
options.description: Should the cluster be present or absent.

options.name: switch_type
options.description: Type of switch to be used by all networks in given cluster. Either I(legacy) which is using linux bridge or I(ovs) using Open vSwitch.

options.name: threads_as_cores
options.description: If I(True) the exposed host threads would be treated as cores which can be utilized by virtual machines.

options.name: timeout
options.description: The amount of time in seconds the module should wait for the instance to get into desired state.

options.name: trusted_service
options.description: If I(True) enables integration with an OpenAttestation server.

options.name: virt
options.description: If I(True), hosts in this cluster will be used to run virtual machines.

options.name: vm_reason
options.description: If I(True) enables an optional reason field when a virtual machine is shut down from the Manager, allowing the administrator to provide an explanation for the maintenance.

options.name: wait
options.description: C(yes) if the module should wait for the entity to get into desired state.
